grounding.derivation: This is a derived local implementation contract, not an imported protocol theorem: PrepareReply declares VBallot; handlePrepare copies inst.vbal into that field; SendMsg invokes Marshal and the receive loop invokes New then Unmarshal; handlePrepareReply uses VBallot to select the highest accepted-value ballot. Omitting or replacing that value changes information explicitly communicated between these callers. No field-normalization step or zero-only restriction appears in these paths. handlePropose uses owner ID as the initial ballot and handlePreAccept records it in vbal, admitting nonzero inputs.
grounding.applicability: The obligation applies independently at the producer/codec boundary. Empty reduced replicas bypass startup and workers, but normal handlers create the instance and the reply. Public codec inputs are unrestricted PrepareReply fields; no whole-cluster history premise is needed for preservation of a message produced by these handlers.
alternatives: A cluster consequence needs a separate compatible history: startRecoveryForInstance also assigns its new ballot to its local self reply, which can dominate remote evidence independently of serialization.

func (t *PrepareReply) Unmarshal(rr io.Reader) error {
	var wire byteReader
	var ok bool
	if wire, ok = rr.(byteReader); !ok {
		wire = bufio.NewReader(rr)
	}
	var b [17]byte
	var bs []byte
	bs = b[:17]
	if _, err := io.ReadAtLeast(wire, bs, 17); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.AcceptorId = int32((uint32(bs[0]) | (uint32(bs[1]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[2]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[3]) << 24)))
	t.Replica = int32((uint32(bs[4]) | (uint32(bs[5]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[6]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[7]) << 24)))
	t.Instance = int32((uint32(bs[8]) | (uint32(bs[9]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[10]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[11]) << 24)))
	t.Ballot = int32((uint32(bs[12]) | (uint32(bs[13]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[14]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[15]) << 24)))
	t.Status = int8(bs[16])
	alen1, err := binary.ReadVarint(wire)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.Command = make([]state.Command, alen1)
	for i := int64(0); i < alen1; i++ {
		t.Command[i].Unmarshal(wire)
	}
	bs = b[:4]
	if _, err := io.ReadAtLeast(wire, bs, 4); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.Seq = int32((uint32(bs[0]) | (uint32(bs[1]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[2]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[3]) << 24)))
	alen2, err := binary.ReadVarint(wire)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.Deps = make([]int32, alen2)
	for i := int64(0); i < alen2; i++ {
		if _, err := io.ReadAtLeast(wire, bs, 4); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		t.Deps[i] = int32((uint32(bs[0]) | (uint32(bs[1]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[2]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[3]) << 24)))
	}
	return nil
}

type PrepareReply struct {
	AcceptorId int32
	Replica    int32
	Instance   int32
	Ballot     int32
	VBallot    int32
	Status     int8
	Command    []state.Command
	Seq        int32
	Deps       []int32
}

	r.acceptRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(Accept), r.acceptChan)
	r.acceptReplyRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(AcceptReply), r.acceptReplyChan)
	r.commitRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(Commit), r.commitChan)
	r.tryPreAcceptRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(TryPreAccept), r.tryPreAcceptChan)
	r.tryPreAcceptReplyRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(TryPreAcceptReply), r.tryPreAcceptReplyChan)

	r.Stats.M["weird"], r.Stats.M["conflicted"], r.Stats.M["slow"], r.Stats.M["fast"], r.Stats.M["totalCommitTime"], r.Stats.M["totalBatching"], r.Stats.M["totalBatchingSize"] = 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0

	go r.run()

	return r
